prerequisites: It is suggested to access the 'PI-Química' Starting Point Chemistry course on the UPM Moodle platform.
Recommended to have previously completed Chemistry subjects in Baccalaureate.
Knowledge of chemical nomenclature and formulation is required.

learning_outcomes.text: Possess the capacity to design, develop, implement, manage, and improve products, systems, and processes in different industrial fields, using appropriate analytical, computational, or experimental techniques.
Apply acquired knowledge to identify, formulate, and solve problems in broad contexts, being capable of integrating them by working in multidisciplinary teams.
Understand the impact of engineering on the environment, the sustainable development of society, and the importance of working in a professional and responsible environment.
Ability to know, understand, and use the principles of general chemistry, organic and inorganic chemistry, and their applications in engineering.
Possess learning skills that allow continuous lifelong learning for adequate professional development.
Know and apply knowledge of basic sciences and technologies to the practice of Industrial Engineering.
Ability for chemical laboratory work, translating theoretical knowledge to the laboratory and relating contents to the real world.
Ability to safely handle chemical products. Recognize and implement good measurement and experimentation practices.
Ability to know, understand, and use the principles of general chemistry.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Chemistry. Stoichiometry
The language of Chemistry. Stoichiometry of chemical reactions.
Ideal gases. Gas mixtures.
Solutions. Ways to express the concentration of a solution.
Structure of matter
Atomic structure. Basic principles of Quantum Mechanics. Electron configurations.
Periodic classification of elements. Periodic properties.
Chemical bonding: Nature of chemical bonding.
Ionic bonding: Lattice energy. Stability of ionic compounds.
Covalent bonding. Geometries of molecules and molecular ions.
Metallic bonding. Conductors, insulators, and semiconductors.
Intermolecular forces: van der Waals forces. Hydrogen bonding.
States of aggregation of matter
Real gases.
Solids: Crystalline and amorphous solids. Classification of solids according to bond type. Real solids.
Liquids: Surface tension. Viscosity. Evaporation and vapor pressure. Real liquids.
Changes of state: Heating and cooling curves. Phase equilibria. Phase diagrams.
Solutions: Solubility. Purification of substances. Colligative properties of solutions.
Fundamentals of chemical reaction. Applications
Energy of chemical reactions. Transformations at constant pressure and volume. Calorimetry. Thermochemistry. Hess's Law. Bond energies. Entropy, Free Energy, and Spontaneous Change.
Chemical equilibrium: Equilibrium constant. Factors affecting chemical equilibrium.
Chemical kinetics: Rate and mechanism of chemical reactions. Factors influencing reaction rate. Rate equation. Determination of rate laws. Catalysis.
Acid-base equilibria: Acid-base theories. Ionization constant. Concept and calculation of pH. Hydrolysis. Buffer solutions. Indicators. Neutralization titrations.
Solubility equilibria: Solubility product. Factors influencing the solubility of ionic compounds.

Oxidation-reduction reactions. Electrochemistry: Redox equations. Redox titrations. Galvanic cells. Standard potential. Spontaneity. Nernst equation. Equilibria in redox reactions. Types of cells. Electrolysis. Corrosion and protection.
Experimental Laboratory Syllabus
Knowledge and handling of Laboratory equipment. Safety rules.
Separation methods. Preparation of solutions.
Heat of reaction.
Chemical equilibrium and the effect of temperature on kinetics.
pH calculation. Titrations.
Oxidation-reduction reactions. Electrochemical phenomena.
Corrosion and cathodic protection tests of iron. Laboratory exam.

assessment_methods.method: Resolution, submission and oral presentation of problems
Study and resolution of questionnaires (Flipped classroom)

assessment_rules: The student passes the course with a final grade equal to or greater than 5 in progressive evaluation, provided that the Laboratory Practices have been completed. The 2nd class exam requires a minimum grade of 4. It is essential to have completed the Laboratory Practices to pass the course. For students who have not passed or not completed the progressive evaluation, a Global Test (ordinary call) will assess all competencies with a 100% exam, provided laboratory practices are completed. An Extraordinary Call exam also evaluates all competencies with a 100% exam under the same condition regarding laboratory practices.
